Alex P: Quick dump from an nsys perf session — reproducer with longseq inputs (>2048) shows an HBM bandwidth collapse coinciding with repeated KV cache evictions. timeline looks like alternating heavy kernel then long idle with small memcpy spikes. :thinking:

Maya R: can you paste the nsys link + the exact cmd you used?

Alex P: nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,cublas -o traces/longseq_hbm --sample=none ./run_infer.sh --model=redwood-7b --seq=4096 --batch=1
Attached timeline: top shows kernels labeled fast_attn_vec and fallback_attn_vec switching frequently. HBM util drops from ~760GB/s to ~120GB/s during those fallback stretches.

Jin L: do you see big PCIe memcpy or GPU->CPU shuffles when the drop happens? could be prefetch backoff.

Alex P: Not large PCIe copies. Perf counters point to lots of L2 misses and subsequent DRAM reads, plus sustained DRAM read latency jumps. Snippet from nvprof-like counters (sampled):
```
DRAM_READ_THROUGHPUT: 720 GB/s -> 115 GB/s
L2_HIT_RATE: 0.62 -> 0.18
SM_ACTIVE: 98% -> 14% (during fallback window)
```

Sam T: that SM_ACTIVE drop is worrying — kernel selection may be picking a scalar fallback kernel for tails. Are we seeing many small threads launched?

Alex P: Exactly. Kernel timelines show many tiny kernels (<300us) that are launch-heavy. The selector switches based on seq len heuristic in runtime: when KV span > X bytes we switch to page-aligned kernel variant that doesn't use the large-block GEMM. For these long sequences the KV writes thrash the HBM allocator and cause eviction waves.

Maya R: Could be two interacting issues: a) selector threshold too aggressive for longseq patterns, b) allocator fragmentation causing smaller contiguous HBM regions -> DMA inefficiencies.

Jin L: Suggest: 1) bump selector to prefer large-block kernel up to longer seqs, 2) enable aggressive prefix KV caching to reduce writes around the tail, 3) re-run perfetto with memtrack enabled to see allocator behavior.

Alex P: I tried option 1 locally: forcing large-block kernel for seq<=8192 removed the tiny-kernel storms and HBM BW stayed ~680 GB/s. Also reduced end-to-end latency by ~12%.

PerfBot: FYI — saved trace at s3://perf/traces/1769994000-longseq_hbm/; flamegraph and kernel timeline available. :thumbsup:

Sam T: Nice. We should add an AB test: change selector threshold behind a flag and run ~1000 longseq requests to measure regression impact on shortseq cases. Also add a metric for consecutive eviction events per minute.

Maya R: I'll open a quick PR to add the flag and default it off. Alex, can you paste the minimal repro script you used (run_infer.sh) in the thread so QE can run it?

Alex P: pasted gist link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf/longseq-repro. It runs synthetic KV-heavy workload hitting NV cache pages repeatedly. Repro steps in the gist.

Jin L: After we confirm, also check kernel microbenchmarks: measure ILP in both kernels and the achieved occupancy. If large-block wins on occupancy and BW, we should prefer it and tune launch dims.

Alex P: Will follow up with perf numbers and sample perfetto memtrack screenshots. Thanks all. :rocket:
